info.title: Karya
info.summary: Multi-tenant staff attendance and presence verification platform.
info.description:
Multi-tenant staff attendance with **server-verified presence**.

Every request is scoped to the authenticated user's own tenant. Identity, role,
tenant, GPS validity, geofence distance, QR validity and the attendance timestamp
are all determined by the server; no client-supplied value influences any of them.

**Authentication.** `POST /api/v1/auth/login` returns a short-lived JWT access
token and a long-lived, revocable refresh token. Send the access token as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Refresh tokens must be rotated - the presented
token is revoked as part of a successful rotation, so replaying one fails.

**Errors.** Every error response is `{"detail": ...}`. Validation failures return
422 with a list of `{type, loc, msg}` under `detail`; the submitted value is never
echoed back. Rate-limited requests return 429 with a `Retry-After` header. Every
response, success or failure, carries an `X-Request-ID` header - quote it when
reporting a problem.

**Presence and attendance refusals are not HTTP errors.** A well-formed request
refused on its merits - outside the geofence, QR already used, already checked in -
returns **200** with `verified: false` or `success: false` and a machine-readable
`reason`. 4xx is reserved for requests that could not be processed at all.

**Nothing is ever deleted.** There is no `DELETE` method anywhere in this API.
Users move between `ACTIVE` and `INACTIVE`; attendance events are immutable.

get.description: Report that the process is running. Never touches the database.
Report whether a trivial query against PostgreSQL succeeds.

503.description: Not ready - a required dependency is unavailable

post.summary: Authenticate within a tenant and obtain tokens
post.description:
Exchange tenant slug + email + password for an access/refresh pair.

Returns the same 401 whether the tenant is unknown, the user is unknown, the
password is wrong, or the account is inactive.

Failed attempts are counted per (tenant, email) and the counter is cleared on
success, so repeated guessing against one account is throttled while a person
who mistypes once and then succeeds is not. The 429 that throttling produces is
identical for an account that exists and one that does not - the
anti-enumeration property has to hold for every status code, not only 401.

post.summary: Rotate a refresh token for a new token pair
post.description:
Rotate the supplied refresh token.

The presented token is revoked as part of a successful rotation, so
presenting it a second time fails. Rejection is never downgraded to
"issue a new token anyway".

Revoke the supplied refresh token.

Idempotent, and returns 204 even for an unknown or already-revoked token so
the endpoint cannot be used to probe which tokens exist. Access tokens are
short-lived and are not blacklisted in this phase.

get.description:
Return the caller's own profile.

Identity comes exclusively from the validated bearer token; any ``user_id``,
``tenant_id`` or ``role`` supplied as a query parameter, header or body is
ignored. The response never includes ``password_hash``.

post.summary: Create a new organization and its first administrator
post.description:
Create a tenant and its first (unverified) TENANT_ADMIN.

The new account cannot sign in until the emailed verification link is
followed - see ``POST /onboarding/verify-email``. Nothing about the new
account is returned here beyond the slug the admin will log in with;
there is no token to hand back, since the account is not usable yet.

409.description: That organization ID is already in use

503.description: Could not send the verification email right now. Try again shortly.

post.summary: Verify an onboarding email address and sign in
post.description:
Activate the account behind a verification token and sign it in.

Returns the same token pair shape as ``POST /auth/login`` - the person
who just proved they own this email address is, at this exact moment,
as authenticated as anyone who just typed a correct password, so there
is no reason to make them do that too.

401, not 404 or 410: a token that never existed, one already consumed,
and one that expired are all indistinguishable to the caller, the same
anti-enumeration posture login itself uses for credentials.

401.description: This verification link is invalid or has expired

post.description:
Issue a fresh verification link for a lost or expired one.

Always returns the same message and 200, whether or not an email was
actually sent - see
:func:`app.services.onboarding.service.resend_verification_email` for
why. Shares `verify-email`'s rate-limit budget: both are unauthenticated,
per-IP, identity-guessing-shaped actions.

The one exception to "always 200" is the mail server itself being
unreachable (`EmailDeliveryError`) - that failure is identical no matter
which organization/email was requested, so surfacing it as a 503 leaks
nothing about whether the account exists.

503.description: Could not send the verification email right now. Try again shortly.

post.summary: Issue a short-lived QR challenge for the office display
post.description:
Mint a new dynamic QR challenge for the caller's own tenant.

The tenant and its attendance location are resolved from the authenticated
user, so a caller cannot issue a challenge for anyone else's site. The
challenge is single-use and expires after the configured TTL; the display is
expected to re-request one shortly before it lapses.

409.description: No active attendance location is configured

post.summary: Issue a short-lived QR challenge, authenticated as a kiosk display
post.description:
The same challenge-issuance endpoint above, for an unattended kiosk.

Identical response shape and identical underlying service call - only the
caller's identity differs. A display token identifies one tenant's one
physical screen, never a person, so the issued challenge is audited with
no actor rather than attributed to whichever admin happened to set the
kiosk up.

409.description: No active attendance location is configured

post.summary: Verify physical presence from GPS and QR evidence
post.description:
Evaluate GPS + QR evidence for the authenticated user.

Open to any authenticated, active user of the tenant - STAFF included, since
proving one's own presence is the normal staff action.

A rejection is returned as **200 with ``verified: false``**, not a 4xx: the
request was well-formed and processed, and the body carries a structured
verdict per signal. HTTP error codes are reserved for requests that could
not be processed at all (401 unauthenticated, 422 malformed evidence).

The commit persists the audit row and, on success, the QR consumption.

Record a CHECK_IN for the authenticated user.

Presence is verified here as part of the action - a prior call to
``/presence/verify`` neither helps nor is trusted. The user must currently
be ``NOT_CHECKED_IN``; a duplicate attempt is refused with
``ALREADY_CHECKED_IN`` and, deliberately, without consuming the QR
challenge.

Record a CHECK_OUT for the authenticated user.

Requires a preceding CHECK_IN: without one the attempt is refused with
``NOT_CHECKED_IN``. Needs its own fresh QR challenge, since the one that
authorised the check-in was consumed by it.

get.summary: The caller's own attendance for a day
get.description:
Return the authenticated user's attendance, defaulting to today (UTC).

Identity comes from the bearer token; a ``user_id`` in the query string, a
header or a body is ignored entirely. There is no way to ask this endpoint
about anybody else.

parameters.name: day

schema.description: UTC date to report on, defaults to today
schema.title: Day

parameters.description: UTC date to report on, defaults to today

get.description: Paginated daily history for the authenticated user, newest day first.

parameters.name: to_date

schema.description: Inclusive end date (UTC), defaults to today
schema.title: To Date

parameters.description: Inclusive end date (UTC), defaults to today

get.summary: Today's attendance across the caller's tenant
get.description:
Every active user in the caller's own tenant, with today's attendance.

The tenant comes from the authenticated user, so there is no parameter that
could widen the query to another tenant. Users with no events still appear,
as ``NO_RECORD`` - they are precisely who a manager is looking for.

parameters.name: day

schema.description: UTC date to report on, defaults to today
schema.title: Day

parameters.description: UTC date to report on, defaults to today

get.summary: One tenant user's attendance for a day
get.description:
Attendance for one user in the caller's own tenant.

A user id belonging to a different tenant returns **404**, identical to an id
that does not exist anywhere. Distinguishing the two would confirm the id is
real and turn this into a cross-tenant enumeration oracle.

parameters.name: day

schema.description: UTC date to report on, defaults to today
schema.title: Day

parameters.description: UTC date to report on, defaults to today

get.description:
Paginated daily history for one user in the caller's own tenant.

Remains available for **inactive** users: they are excluded from the live
dashboard, but their recorded history is an audit record and is never hidden
or deleted.

parameters.name: to_date

schema.description: Inclusive end date (UTC), defaults to today
schema.title: To Date

parameters.description: Inclusive end date (UTC), defaults to today

get.description:
Return the authenticated user's profile.

Identity comes from the bearer token; no id is accepted. Never includes
``password_hash`` or any token.

patch.description:
Update the caller's own safe profile fields.

Only ``name`` is writable here. Role, status, tenant and email are not - they
are administrative or identity concerns, and a schema that never declares them
rejects an attempt to send one with a 422.

post.description:
Change the authenticated user's password.

The current password is verified before anything about the new one is
considered, so the endpoint answers no questions for a caller who has not
proven they own the account. A wrong current password returns 401 with a
generic message - never a hint about the new password's acceptability.

Every refresh session is revoked on success: a password change usually means
the old one is suspect, and a 30-day refresh token would otherwise keep
whoever knew it signed in.

401.description: Not authenticated, or current password incorrect

post.summary: Create a user in the caller's tenant
post.description:
Create a user inside the administrator's own tenant.

The tenant is taken from the authenticated administrator - there is no
``tenant_id`` field, so a user cannot be created anywhere else. The password is
hashed with Argon2id and never echoed back.

A duplicate email or employee code surfaces as a clean 409; the underlying
constraint violation never reaches the client.

409.description: Email or employee code already in use

get.summary: List users in the caller's tenant
get.description:
One page of the caller's own tenant's users.

Filtering and search happen in SQL - the tenant is never loaded into memory to
be sifted - and the search term is a bound parameter, so wildcards and quotes
are matched literally rather than altering the query. Page size is capped.

get.summary: Read one user in the caller's tenant
get.description:
Read one user from the caller's own tenant.

An id belonging to another tenant returns 404, identical to an id that exists
nowhere - distinguishing them would confirm the id is real and allow
cross-tenant enumeration.

patch.description:
Update a user's profile fields.

Writable: ``email``, ``name``, ``employee_code``. Not writable here: ``role``
and ``status``, which have dedicated endpoints so a privilege change is never
indistinguishable from a typo correction in the audit trail.

409.description: Email or employee code already in use

patch.description:
Change a user's role within the caller's tenant.

Refused if the target is the caller: nobody edits their own role, which closes
the most direct escalation path. Also refused if it would demote the tenant's
last active administrator. ``SUPER_ADMIN`` is not an assignable role.

403.description: Insufficient permissions, or changing your own role

409.description: Would leave the tenant without an administrator

post.description:
Deactivate a user - a lifecycle change, never a delete.

The account can no longer log in, refresh, check in or check out, and its
refresh sessions are revoked immediately. Attendance events and audit rows are
untouched, so history stays complete and still resolves to a real identity.

409.description: Would leave the tenant without an administrator

post.description:
Reactivate a user, restoring their ability to authenticate.

Their password is left alone - reactivation is not a credential reset, and
silently clearing one would lock the person out instead.

get.description:
Lifecycle audit rows for one user, newest first.

Scoped to the tenant, to ``target_type='User'`` and to this user, so it is not
a window onto the tenant's whole audit log - attendance and QR rows are not
reachable here. The metadata contains only identifiers and before/after values.

Return the tenant the authenticated user belongs to.

Open to any active user: knowing which organisation you work for is not
privileged. The response carries no user counts, credentials or configuration.

patch.description:
Update the tenant's display name.

Only ``name``. ``slug`` is excluded despite looking like ordinary metadata: it
is the identifier every employee types at login, so renaming it would lock out
the whole company at once.

get.description:
Return the tenant's attendance location, if one has been set up.

Open to any active user, like ``GET /tenant/me`` - the office address and
geofence radius are operational context, not privileged configuration.

404.description: No attendance location is configured yet

post.summary: Set up the caller's attendance location
post.description:
Create the tenant's one attendance location.

Karya V1 supports exactly one per tenant (see
`app.models.attendance_location`); call ``PATCH`` instead once one
exists. Without this, check-in/out can never succeed for a fresh
tenant - GPS verification has no geofence to test against.

409.description: An attendance location already exists for this tenant

patch.description: Update the tenant's existing attendance location.

404.description: No attendance location is configured yet

get.description:
Never includes a raw token - only what was true at creation time plus
each kiosk's revocation/heartbeat state, enough to decide which to revoke.

post.summary: Mint a credential for one office-display kiosk
post.description:
Mint a new kiosk credential. The raw token is returned exactly once.

Store it in the kiosk's browser immediately - there is no way to
retrieve it again, only to revoke it and mint a replacement.

409.description: Set up your attendance location before creating a display

post.description:
Immediately and permanently disable one kiosk's credential.

404, not 403, for a display token belonging to another tenant - the same
"cross-tenant lookups don't exist" posture every other admin route uses.

post.summary: A kiosk revokes its own credential
post.description:
Let a kiosk disable itself - the "Reset this display" control.

Deliberately narrow: a display token can revoke only the one row its own
token identifies (`display.display_token_id`, derived from the token
itself, never a request parameter - the same "identity is derived, not
accepted" posture every tenant-scoped route already uses), so a leaked
display token gains no capability beyond killing itself. There is no
"un-revoke" - a reset kiosk needs a freshly minted token from an admin,
same as any other revoked display.

AttendanceActionRequest.title: AttendanceActionRequest
AttendanceActionRequest.description:
Evidence for a check-in or check-out.

Identical to the presence contract: coordinates, accuracy, challenge id and
nonce. Note what is *absent* - no user, no tenant, no timestamp, no event
type and no verdict. Those are all determined by the server, and inherited
``extra="forbid"`` turns an attempt to supply one into a 422 rather than a
silently ignored field.

AttendanceActionResponse.title: AttendanceActionResponse
AttendanceActionResponse.description:
The outcome of a check-in or check-out attempt.

A refusal is reported as ``success: false`` with HTTP 200, matching
``/presence/verify``. The request was well-formed and fully processed; the
answer is "no, and here is exactly why". Returning the presence breakdown
alongside the reason is what lets a client tell the user *"you are 350 m
away"* rather than just *"failed"*. HTTP error codes stay reserved for
requests that could not be processed at all - 401 unauthenticated, 422
malformed or smuggled fields.

AttendanceDayResponse.title: AttendanceDayResponse
AttendanceDayResponse.description:
One user's attendance for one UTC calendar day.

``NO_RECORD`` means no attendance event was recorded - **not** that the
person was absent from work. Karya cannot distinguish leave, travel, or a
failure to reach the QR display.

AttendanceHistoryResponse.title: AttendanceHistoryResponse
AttendanceHistoryResponse.description:
A page of daily attendance, newest day first.

Every date in the requested range appears, including days with no events, so
a calendar can distinguish "nothing recorded" from "outside the range".

AttendanceLocationCreateRequest.title: AttendanceLocationCreateRequest
AttendanceLocationCreateRequest.description: Body for ``POST /api/v1/tenant/me/location``. Fails 409 if one exists.

AttendanceLocationUpdateRequest.title: AttendanceLocationUpdateRequest
AttendanceLocationUpdateRequest.description: Body for ``PATCH /api/v1/tenant/me/location``. Fails 404 if none exists.

AttendanceSessionResponse.title: AttendanceSessionResponse
AttendanceSessionResponse.description:
One check-in/check-out pair.

Either side may be ``null``: an open session has no ``check_out``, and a
session that began the previous day (a night shift) has no ``check_in`` on
the day it closes.

AttendanceState.title: AttendanceState
AttendanceState.description:
A user's current attendance state.

Derived from their most recent attendance event - there is deliberately no
``current_status`` column. A denormalised status would be a second source of
truth that can drift from the events, and the events are the audit record
that matters.

``CHECK_OUT`` returns a user to ``NOT_CHECKED_IN``, which is what allows
repeated day-after-day cycles without any reset step.

AttendanceTodayResponse.title: AttendanceTodayResponse
AttendanceTodayResponse.description: The caller's (or a named user's) attendance for a single day.

DayStatus.title: DayStatus
DayStatus.description:
How one calendar day looks for one user.

``NO_RECORD`` is named carefully. It states only that **no attendance event
was recorded** for that day - it is *not* a claim that the person was absent
from work. They may have been on leave, travelling, working elsewhere, or
simply unable to reach the QR display; Karya has no way to tell, and leave
and shift management do not exist yet. "ABSENT" would assert something the
data does not support.

Distinct from :class:`AttendanceState`, which is the *live* state machine
Phase 4 uses to accept or refuse a check-in. This enum describes a completed
(or in-progress) day and therefore needs the third ``COMPLETED`` value.

DisplayTokenCreateResponse.title: DisplayTokenCreateResponse
DisplayTokenCreateResponse.description: Returned once, on creation. The raw token is never retrievable again.

DisplayTokenResponse.title: DisplayTokenResponse
DisplayTokenResponse.description: One row in the listing - never the raw token.

FailureReason.title: FailureReason
FailureReason.description:
Why a presence attempt was rejected.

Some values are internal-only; see :data:`CLIENT_SAFE_REASON` for the
mapping applied before a reason reaches an API response.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description:
Credentials for ``POST /api/v1/auth/login``.

The tenant is identified by slug: login is tenant-scoped, and the user
lookup is constrained to the resolved tenant.

PaginationResponse.title: PaginationResponse
PaginationResponse.description: Page metadata. ``total`` counts **days** in the range, not events.

PasswordChangeRequest.title: PasswordChangeRequest
PasswordChangeRequest.description:
A self-service password change.

No user id: the account is always the authenticated caller, so there is no
field through which an administrator could set someone else's password.

PresenceStatus.title: PresenceStatus
PresenceStatus.description:
Outcome of a presence-verification attempt.

Only two outcomes exist in Phase 3. ``MANUAL_REVIEW`` deliberately does not
appear here: it belongs to ``AttendanceEvent.verification_status``, where
Phase 4 can apply policy to a rejected-but-plausible attempt. Adding a third
presence outcome now would be complexity with no consumer.

PresenceSummary.title: PresenceSummary
PresenceSummary.description: The presence evidence behind an attendance decision.

PresenceVerificationRequest.title: PresenceVerificationRequest
PresenceVerificationRequest.description:
Evidence submitted by a staff device.

Note what is absent: no identity, no tenant, no verdict, no distance. All of
those are derived from the bearer token and the database.

PresenceVerificationResponse.title: PresenceVerificationResponse
PresenceVerificationResponse.description: The presence decision returned to the caller.

QRChallengeResponse.title: QRChallengeResponse
QRChallengeResponse.description:
A freshly issued challenge, for the office display to render as a QR.

The display encodes ``challenge_id`` and ``nonce`` into the QR image; those
two are all a phone needs to submit. Nothing else about the tenant, the
location or its coordinates is included - the server stays authoritative and
the QR stays compact.

QRVerificationResult.title: QRVerificationResult
QRVerificationResult.description: QR challenge outcome. Deliberately carries no nonce.

ResendVerificationRequest.title: ResendVerificationRequest
ResendVerificationRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/onboarding/resend-verification``.

Identifies the account the same way login does - organization slug plus
email - rather than a stale token, since the whole point is recovering
from a link that's gone missing or expired.

message.title: Message
message.default: If that account needs verifying, we've sent a new link.

ResendVerificationResponse.title: ResendVerificationResponse
ResendVerificationResponse.description:
Always the same message, whether or not anything was actually sent -
see :func:`app.services.onboarding.service.resend_verification_email`.

RoleUpdateRequest.title: RoleUpdateRequest
RoleUpdateRequest.description: A role change, on its own dedicated endpoint.

SelfUpdateRequest.title: SelfUpdateRequest
SelfUpdateRequest.description:
Profile fields a user may change about themselves.

Narrower than the administrator's version: no email, because it is the login
identity - changing it unilaterally is how somebody locks themselves out, and
it belongs to the tenant's administration. No employee code either, since the
tenant assigns it.

TeamAttendanceMember.title: TeamAttendanceMember
TeamAttendanceMember.description:
One colleague on the tenant dashboard.

Identity is limited to what a manager needs to recognise the person. Email is
deliberately omitted - it is contact data, not attendance data.

TeamAttendanceResponse.title: TeamAttendanceResponse
TeamAttendanceResponse.description: Today's attendance across the caller's own tenant.

TeamAttendanceSummary.title: TeamAttendanceSummary
TeamAttendanceSummary.description: Headcount by status. The three buckets always sum to ``total_staff``.

TenantOnboardingRequest.title: TenantOnboardingRequest
TenantOnboardingRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/onboarding/tenants``.

Creates a new tenant and its first administrator in one transaction. The
administrator is created ``INACTIVE`` and cannot sign in until the email
address is verified - see
:func:`app.services.onboarding.service.create_tenant_with_admin`.

message.title: Message
message.default: Check your email to verify your account before signing in.

TenantOnboardingResponse.title: TenantOnboardingResponse
TenantOnboardingResponse.description: Deliberately carries no token: the account is not usable yet.

TenantUpdateRequest.title: TenantUpdateRequest
TenantUpdateRequest.description:
The only tenant field a tenant administrator may change.

``slug`` is excluded even though it is human-readable metadata: it is the
tenant identifier every user types at login, so changing it would silently
lock out an entire company. ``status`` is excluded because tenant suspension
is an operator action, not a self-service one. ``id`` and the timestamps are
not writable anywhere.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
Credentials returned by login and refresh.

``refresh_token`` is the only time the raw value is ever exposed; the server
keeps just its hash.

UserAuditEntryResponse.title: UserAuditEntryResponse
UserAuditEntryResponse.description:
One lifecycle audit row.

``metadata`` carries only identifiers and before/after values written by
:mod:`app.services.users.service` - never a password, hash, token or nonce.

UserAuditResponse.title: UserAuditResponse
UserAuditResponse.description: A page of one user's lifecycle audit history.

UserCreateRequest.title: UserCreateRequest
UserCreateRequest.description:
Fields a tenant administrator may supply when creating a user.

``tenant_id`` is absent by design - the tenant comes from the authenticated
administrator, so a user can only ever be created inside the caller's own
tenant.

UserDetailResponse.title: UserDetailResponse
UserDetailResponse.description:
A user as returned by the management endpoints.

Extends :class:`UserResponse` with lifecycle timestamps, which an
administrator needs to see. Still an explicit allowlist - it inherits the
named fields rather than serialising the ORM object, so a column added later
cannot leak.

UserListPagination.title: UserListPagination
UserListPagination.description: Page metadata for a user listing.

UserListResponse.title: UserListResponse
UserListResponse.description: One page of the caller's own tenant's users.

UserResponse.title: UserResponse
UserResponse.description:
The authenticated user, as returned by ``GET /api/v1/auth/me``.

Deliberately excludes ``password_hash`` and every other authentication
artefact. ``created_at``/``updated_at`` are omitted too - nothing needs them
yet, and the narrower the response, the less there is to leak.

UserRole.title: UserRole
UserRole.description: Roles a user may hold. Enforcement (RBAC) is a later phase.

UserStatus.title: UserStatus
UserStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a user account.

UserUpdateRequest.title: UserUpdateRequest
UserUpdateRequest.description:
Profile fields a tenant administrator may change.

Deliberately excludes ``role`` and ``status``: those are lifecycle and
privilege changes with their own endpoints, their own authorization and their
own audit actions. Folding them into a generic update would make a privilege
change indistinguishable from a typo correction in the audit trail.

PATCH semantics: every field is optional and only what is sent is written.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Liveness and readiness probes. Unauthenticated, and deliberately uninformative: `/health` never touches the database, `/ready` does.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Login, refresh-token rotation, logout and the caller's own profile. Every credential failure returns the same 401, so neither a tenant nor a user can be enumerated.

tags.name: presence
tags.description: GPS and dynamic-QR presence verification. Issuing a QR challenge is restricted to MANAGER and TENANT_ADMIN; verifying presence is open to any active user. A QR challenge is single-use and short-lived.

tags.name: attendance
tags.description: Check-in, check-out and read-only attendance views. Presence is re-verified server-side as part of every check-in and check-out. Reading another user's attendance requires MANAGER or TENANT_ADMIN.

tags.name: users
tags.description: Self-service account endpoints, open to any active user, and user administration, restricted to TENANT_ADMIN. MANAGER has no user-management powers.
